candidate.answerReason: Only two yellow balls are available, so any draw of three balls contains at least one white ball.

methods.label: Using the limit on yellow balls
methods.explanation: There are only 2 yellow balls, so drawing 3 balls must include at least 1 white ball. Thus, B is certain to occur; A and C may or may not occur, and D is impossible.
methods.levelReason: The argument uses a simple quantity constraint to establish certainty, within Grade 9 event classification.

candidate.changeReason: Three drawn balls cannot all be yellow because the bag contains only two yellow balls. Drawing all three white balls is possible, so yellow is not guaranteed. The current explanation correctly identifies B.

review.mathematicalCheck: A simultaneous draw of three distinct balls cannot contain only yellow balls because only two exist, so B is certain and D is impossible. Both three white balls and mixed-color draws are possible, making A and C uncertain. B is uniquely correct.
